<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Record ToolParser invocation metrics for direct/shared ParserEngine execution while retaining required/named tool-choice boundaries. Refreshed against main `c5f8adc0` and current ParserManager adapter composition.

## Claims

- Resolve the upstream protocol/renderer import conflicts without restoring the removed ParserManager adapter-collapse optimization.
- Retain direct-engine metrics, reasoning/no-tools exclusions, exception outcomes, and manager-created streaming/non-streaming required/named coverage.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py -v` — **155 passed**.
- The direct-engine Prometheus regression fails against unmodified main production code (counter `0` instead of `1`).
- Pre-commit on both changed files and `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — **passed**.
- These are CPU parser tests. No current-head end-to-end model-serving run was performed; CUDA cannot initialize.

## Details

The original #53359 report concerned manager-created collapsed engines. Upstream has since removed that collapse, so this PR must not be described as a fresh reproduction of the original serving route. The remaining instrumentation applies to direct/shared engine entry points, and the manager-level tests preserve the established ToolParser metric boundary. Maintainer confirmation that this remaining scope is wanted is still needed, as noted by @RichardoMrMu.

Duplicate/coordination check: no competing open PR directly referencing #53359 was found. The earlier coordination request from frank-suwen on the issue remains relevant; this refresh does not claim exclusive ownership. #51814 covers the metrics module rather than these entry points.

Open since 2026-08-22. AI assistance was used for the refresh and validation; commits are signed and signed off with Codex attribution. Human review of the scope and diff remains required.

nodes.body: @RichardoMrMu Thank you for the careful review and for pointing out this semantic issue. We agree that the current instrumentation can count parser-engine calls outside the documented ToolParser invocation boundary. We will update the implementation and regression tests to preserve the existing metric semantics and provide the revised code shortly.

Thanks — exact head `84a3a4e46e168de148c366defbbb2110f8c57d77` closes the `enable_auto_tools=False` and reasoning-only examples, but one reachable legacy boundary still differs for `required` and named choices. `ParserEngineToolAdapter` inherits `supports_required_and_named=True`. In `DelegatingParser`, those branches use the standard JSON / `extract_required_tool_call_streaming` / `extract_named_tool_call_streaming` paths and never call the instrumented `ToolParser.extract_*`, so this counter stays unchanged. When compatible adapters collapse to `ParserEngine`, `parse()` records whenever `enable_auto_tools and _has_tool_parser`, and `parse_delta()` records on CONTENT/tool states, so the same required/named request increments it. That still expands a metric documented as `Total number of ToolParser invocations.` The added tests cover auto but not required/named. Please preserve that choice-specific boundary (or explicitly redefine the metric) and add non-streaming and streaming regressions. The auto/no-tools/reasoning changes otherwise address the original examples. I did not run the suite locally, so I’m not making an independent runtime-suite claim; this part of the semantic-boundary finding remains open.

Rechecked exact head e4ae13196407908d2b3398870e515cb496d27db5: this closes the remaining required/named metric-boundary finding. The selected ToolParser capability is now propagated to the shared engine, and both streaming and non-streaming paths use the same predicate: adapters that support standard required/named handling do not increment the ToolParser counter, while adapters that must fall back to ToolParser still do. The new required/named x capability tests cover both paths. Thanks for carrying this through.

I validated the source and focused control flow; I did not run the full suite, so this is finding closure rather than a CI or merge-readiness claim.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @ActiveSky.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Rechecked exact head `332c3982a62fb014c42078c80e3c0b16825c5f25` after the rebase. The original required/named metric-boundary finding remains closed, but the basis changed: upstream `46638857` removed `ParserManager`'s compatible-adapter collapse, so current production construction preserves the selected adapter and the existing `DelegatingParser` boundary still distinguishes standard required/named handling from ToolParser fallback in both streaming and non-streaming modes.

One merge-readiness caveat follows from that change: the direct `ParserEngine` metric matrix now validates defensive entry points rather than the manager-created production route. Before merge, it may be worth confirming whether the new `ParserEngine` instrumentation is still needed or has been superseded; if retained, one `ParserManager`-created end-to-end metric regression covering streaming/non-streaming required/named standard versus fallback would make the serving contract explicit. The current `pre-run-check` failure is the readiness-label gate; no functional unit suite has run on this head.

This updates my earlier exact-head closure note; I am not reopening the finding.

@RichardoMrMu Thank you for taking another careful look and for clarifying how the upstream `ParserManager` change affects the production path. We agree that the current direct `ParserEngine` matrix does not fully cover the manager-created route.

As a next step, we plan to keep the current instrumentation for direct and compatibility entry points, and add a manager-level regression covering streaming and non-streaming required/named choices for both standard handling and ToolParser fallback. We will run the focused tests and update the PR accordingly. Thanks again for the detailed review.

Hello @aarnphm @chaunceyjiang @sfeng33 @bbrowning, when you have a chance, could you please review this PR? It restores engine-backed parser invocation metrics. Any feedback or guidance on the current implementation and regression coverage would be greatly appreciated. Thank you for your time!

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @ActiveSky.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Hi @bbrowning @chaunceyjiang @aarnphm @sfeng33 @RichardoMrMu, I merged main `c5f8adc0` and resolved the protocol/renderer import conflicts, retaining the manager-created streaming/non-streaming required/named metric coverage requested in review.

Validation: **155 parser tests passed** and pre-commit passed. Main still fails the direct-engine Prometheus regression (`0` rather than `1`). These are CPU tests, not an end-to-end serving validation.

This PR has been open since **August 22**, but upstream has removed the original ParserManager collapse route. The refreshed description therefore limits the remaining claim to direct/shared engine entry points and asks whether that instrumentation is still wanted. I also noted frank-suwen's earlier coordination request on #53359 and am happy to consolidate effort. Could you please review the remaining scope and the updated coverage so we can settle the next step? Thank you.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

This moves the instrumented boundary from actual `ToolParser` calls to normal `ParserEngine.parse()` / `parse_delta()` execution after history initialization, once parser metrics are registered. The new Prometheus test explicitly counts a method-level no-tools call (`tools=None`, `tool_choice=none`, `enable_auto_tools=False`): base=0, legacy=0, head=1. A reasoning-only `parse_delta()` likewise changes 0 to 1 while legacy code remains in its reasoning phase. The direct no-tools case is not established as reachable through standard serving, but the reasoning-only case applies when compatible reasoning/tool adapters collapse to one engine. Could we either preserve the legacy tool-parser boundary or explicitly redefine/document this as parser-engine invocation telemetry?

issue_comments.body: @RichardoMrMu Thank you for the careful review and for pointing out this semantic issue. We agree that the current instrumentation can count parser-engine calls outside the documented ToolParser invocation boundary. We will update the implementation and regression tests to preserve the existing metric semantics and provide the revised code shortly.

Thanks — exact head `84a3a4e46e168de148c366defbbb2110f8c57d77` closes the `enable_auto_tools=False` and reasoning-only examples, but one reachable legacy boundary still differs for `required` and named choices. `ParserEngineToolAdapter` inherits `supports_required_and_named=True`. In `DelegatingParser`, those branches use the standard JSON / `extract_required_tool_call_streaming` / `extract_named_tool_call_streaming` paths and never call the instrumented `ToolParser.extract_*`, so this counter stays unchanged. When compatible adapters collapse to `ParserEngine`, `parse()` records whenever `enable_auto_tools and _has_tool_parser`, and `parse_delta()` records on CONTENT/tool states, so the same required/named request increments it. That still expands a metric documented as `Total number of ToolParser invocations.` The added tests cover auto but not required/named. Please preserve that choice-specific boundary (or explicitly redefine the metric) and add non-streaming and streaming regressions. The auto/no-tools/reasoning changes otherwise address the original examples. I did not run the suite locally, so I’m not making an independent runtime-suite claim; this part of the semantic-boundary finding remains open.

Rechecked exact head e4ae13196407908d2b3398870e515cb496d27db5: this closes the remaining required/named metric-boundary finding. The selected ToolParser capability is now propagated to the shared engine, and both streaming and non-streaming paths use the same predicate: adapters that support standard required/named handling do not increment the ToolParser counter, while adapters that must fall back to ToolParser still do. The new required/named x capability tests cover both paths. Thanks for carrying this through.

I validated the source and focused control flow; I did not run the full suite, so this is finding closure rather than a CI or merge-readiness claim.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

This moves the instrumented boundary from actual `ToolParser` calls to normal `ParserEngine.parse()` / `parse_delta()` execution after history initialization, once parser metrics are registered. The new Prometheus test explicitly counts a method-level no-tools call (`tools=None`, `tool_choice=none`, `enable_auto_tools=False`): base=0, legacy=0, head=1. A reasoning-only `parse_delta()` likewise changes 0 to 1 while legacy code remains in its reasoning phase. The direct no-tools case is not established as reachable through standard serving, but the reasoning-only case applies when compatible reasoning/tool adapters collapse to one engine. Could we either preserve the legacy tool-parser boundary or explicitly redefine/document this as parser-engine invocation telemetry?
